title: Quiz: Setting Up the R Modelling Environment

questions.text: After loading the MASS package, which line should you run immediately to avoid broken dplyr pipelines?
questions.explanation: MASS exports select() and filter() which overwrite dplyr's versions. Reassigning select <- dplyr::select and filter <- dplyr::filter restores the tidyverse functions.

questions.text: The splines package must be installed separately using install.packages('splines') before you can use ns().
questions.explanation: splines ships with base R — it is always available. You only need to call library(splines) to make ns() accessible; no install.packages() step is needed.

questions.text: What is the purpose of setting options(na.action = na.warn)?
options: It causes lm() to stop with an error if any NA values are present
It replaces all NA values with the column mean before fitting
It prints a warning whenever modelling functions silently drop rows with missing values
It removes the NA values from the dataset permanently
questions.explanation: na.warn issues a message when rows are dropped due to NA, making the data loss visible. Without it, rows are silently omitted, which can cause subtle bugs in downstream analysis.

questions.text: Which modelr dataset has a categorical predictor x?
questions.explanation: sim2 has a categorical x variable, making it the right dataset for exploring dummy coding and categorical predictors in Module 4.

questions.text: Putting install.packages() inside a chunk with eval=FALSE ensures the packages are reinstalled every time the document is knitted.
questions.explanation: eval=FALSE means the chunk is shown in the output but NOT executed when knitting. The packages are not reinstalled — they are only installed when the user manually runs that specific chunk.
